findings.problem: Line 7's joke doesn't match the action it's meant to show. The point is hearing Jesus' words and not acting on them (Luke 6:46-49). But someone who 'read the instructions twice and still burned the batch' did bake. They acted and got it wrong. That isn't someone who heard and did nothing. The comparison needs the same action, like someone who reads the recipe and never turns the oven on.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Line 5 starts with 'Because what's inside is what comes out.' Right after line 4 (speck and beam, Luke 6:41-42), this makes the trees-and-fruit teaching (Luke 6:43-45) the reason for checking your own eye first. The BSB never links the two. Luke 6:43 starts with no connecting word, and the 'For' in Luke 6:44 only links verse 44 to verse 43.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Nothing in the Big Idea covers the parable of the blind man leading a blind man or the disciple and his teacher (Luke 6:39-40). Luke calls this 'a parable,' and it's part of the sermon. Every other section of the sermon gets a mention.

rule.text: It covers the whole passage, including any included parable or sermon.

findings.problem: Line 2 says 'love your enemies, give without keeping score, lend expecting nothing in return' but gives only one reference, Luke 6:35, for the quote at the end. 'Give without keeping score' comes from Luke 6:30 (and 6:38), and 'love your enemies' first comes in Luke 6:27. None of these carry a reference.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The Big Idea leaves out the opening scene in Luke 6:17-19: Jesus comes down to a level place, a huge crowd comes from Judea, Jerusalem, Tyre and Sidon to hear Him and be healed, and power comes from Him and heals them all. Line 1 opens with 'here's the whole sermon in one box' and goes straight to the Beatitudes.
findings.question: In a Sermons passage, does 'covers the whole passage' mean the Big Idea must also mention the setting verses before the sermon starts (here the healings in Luke 6:17-19), or is covering the sermon itself enough?
